prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Management determined a provision for credit losses of $40,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was appropriate compared to no provision for credit losses during the same period last year. Management determined that an increase in provision for loan losses for the quarter just ended was appropriate in light of the current economic environment and the recent increase in the overnight interest rate made by the Federal Open Market Committee. While the current economic indicators present a mixed bag of positive and negative attributes, the recent interest rate increase and market sentiment about future interest rate increases may increase pressure on borrowers and, therefore, impact our loan portfolio.

Kentucky First Federal Bancorp MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (continued)

Comparison of Operating Results for the Three-month Periods Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (continued)

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
Non-interest expense decreased $130,000 or 5.9% and totaled $2.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to decreased outside service fees, other non-interest expense, FDIC insurance premiums, and employee compensation and benefits.

Outside service fees decreased $55,000 or 34.4% due to the reduction in the utilization of third party services period to period, which was primarily the result of the completion of third party services associated with the Company’s efforts to address the requirements in the Formal Agreement with the OCC, which was terminated. Other non-interest expense decreased $41,000 or 24.7% due to other employee expense decreasing as the Company discontinued its use of a placement service to identify management level employee candidates. FDIC insurance premiums decreased $19,000 or 31.1% due to First Federal of Kentucky’s no longer being under formal agreement with the OCC, which lowered that bank’s premiums. Employee compensation and benefits decreased $12,000 due chiefly to having 3 less full-time employees from period to period.

nonop.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonop.text:
Non-interest expense decreased $130,000 or 5.9% and totaled $2.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to decreased outside service fees, other non-interest expense, FDIC insurance premiums, and employee compensation and benefits.

Outside service fees decreased $55,000 or 34.4% due to the reduction in the utilization of third party services period to period, which was primarily the result of the completion of third party services associated with the Company’s efforts to address the requirements in the Formal Agreement with the OCC, which was terminated. Other non-interest expense decreased $41,000 or 24.7% due to other employee expense decreasing as the Company discontinued its use of a placement service to identify management level employee candidates. FDIC insurance premiums decreased $19,000 or 31.1% due to First Federal of Kentucky’s no longer being under formal agreement with the OCC, which lowered that bank’s premiums. Employee compensation and benefits decreased $12,000 due chiefly to having 3 less full-time employees from period to period.

net.text: Net income totaled $919,000 or $0.11 diluted earnings per share for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $575,000 from net income of $344,000 or $0.04 diluted earnings per share for the same period in 2025. The increase in net earnings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was primarily attributable to increased net interest income and decreased non-interest expense.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income increased $639,000 or 25.5% to $3.1 million due primarily to both increased interest income and decreased interest expense. Interest income increased $159,000 or 3.1%, while interest expense decreased $480,000 or 18.8% to $2.1 million for the recently-ended quarter.

The average rate earned on interest-earning assets increased 38 basis points to 5.97% and was the primary reason for the increase in interest income, outweighing the decrease in average interest earning assets of $12.6 million or 3.5% to $349.1 million for the recently-ended quarterly period. The increase in interest income was due primarily to an increase of $249,000 or 5.3% in interest income from loans, which totaled $4.9 million for the period.

The increase in interest income from loans period-to-period was due to average rate earned on loans increasing 47 basis points to 6.18%. The average balance of loans decreased $8.9 million or 2.7% to $319.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

While average total interest-bearing liabilities decreased $13.4 million or 4.4%, the primary reason for decreased interest expense was the decrease in the average rate paid on interest bearing liabilities, decreasing 50 basis points to 2.82% for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026.

intro.text: Certain statements contained in this report, as well as other periodic reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, that are not historical facts are considered “forward-looking statements” under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, that are subject to certain risks and uncertainties. These forward-looking statements may be identified by the use of words such as “believe,” “expect,” “anticipate,” “plan,” “estimate,” “intend” and “potential,” or words of similar meaning, or future or conditional verbs such as “should,” “could,” or “may.” Forward-looking statements include statements of our goals, intentions and expectations; statements regarding our business plans, prospects, growth and operating strategies; statements regarding the quality of our loan and investment portfolios; and estimates of our risks and future costs and benefits.

s.t: The primary sources of employment are public administration, education, other services, and health care.
The primary sources of employment are health care, retail, information services, and manufacturing.
The primary sources of employment are education, health care, retail, and construction.
Payments on loans secured by income properties often depend on successful operation and management of the properties.
The primary source of loan originations are our in-house loan originators, and to a lesser extent, advertising and referrals from customers and real estate agents.
Deposits, loan repayments and maturities, redemptions, sales and repayments of investment and mortgage-backed securities are the major sources of our funds for lending and other investment purposes.
The OCC is required to take certain supervisory actions against undercapitalized federal savings associations, the severity of which depends upon the association’s degree of undercapitalization.
An institution’s assessment rate depends upon the category to which it is assigned, and certain adjustments specified by FDIC regulations.
Our operations rely on the secure processing, storage, and transmission of confidential and other information in our computer systems and networks.
We rely on standard Internet security systems to provide the security and authentication necessary to effect secure transmission of data.
We also are required to maintain an investment in FHLB-Cincinnati stock, the level of which is largely dependent on our level of borrowings from the FHLB.
